newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor woes are not political - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Koor woes are not political - analysts.

text.p: A fall in earnings at Israel's Koor Industries Ltd was caused by the construction sector and lower profits at an electronics unit rather than a deteriorating economic and political environment, analysts said.

"It's almost too much," said Elise Horowitz, an analyst at Lehman Brothers in London, referring to Koor's contention that Israel's deteriorating political and economic climate had been responsible for the 9.6 percent decline in third-quarter net earnings to $31.3 million.
"They keep attacking the current government, which inherited the problems from the previous government," she said.

"This is probably the best third quarter I've seen in a couple of years (for Israeli companies)," added another analyst for a European investment house, who asked not to be identified. "The economic and political business doesn't hold water."
Both analysts said Koor's problems were in its building-materials business, particularly Nesher cement, and in its Telrad Telecommunication and Electronic Industries Ltd unit.
The closure of the West Bank and Gaza have reduced cement sales to the regions while residential building starts in Israel have been falling this year.

The European analyst said he expected Nesher's problems would continue to affect Koor in coming quarters, with the added threat of Jordanian cement imports starting to enter the Israeli market, where Nesher is a monopoly.
"Any trade agreement with Jordan that allows for the free flow of cement is bad for Nesher," he said.

Meanwhile, Telrad is facing pressure on margins from its chief customer Bezeq Israel Telecom, they said. Bezeq has forced Telrad and Tadiran Ltd to cut prices for the telephone switching stations they sell, but Tadiran has a much broader product base and has not felt the pinch.

Horowitz said Koor felt the same pressures at Nesher and Telrad in 1995, but fast earnings growth at Tadiran had offset them. "Now Tadiran is moving along nicely, but it is not proving the great expectations previous realised," she said.

Horowitz said she did not expect any immediate improvement in Koor's profits. "The (fourth) quarter will mirror this quarter -- a continued improvement in agro-chemcial sales and continued pressure on building materials," she said. "Tadiran will be okay."
Horowitz said she was lowering her 1997 revenue forecasts for Koor, but holding to her earnings per share outlook of 41.11 shekels because of expected increases in capital gains and other income.
